headline: Electronics rebound and Basler deal drive profit surge
summary_short: Revenue rose 20.4% y/y to $738.8M on Electronics-segment volume strength and the Basler acquisition, while net income jumped 55.9% to $89.4M as gross margin expanded 360bp to 41.4%.
summary_long: Net sales rose 20.4% y/y to $738.8M, including $35.8M of incremental Basler revenue and higher Electronics volume ($44.7M electronics products, $26.1M semiconductor) on stronger demand and price. Gross margin expanded 360bp to 41.4% on volume leverage, execution, and favorable mix. GAAP operating income rose 29.0% to $119.7M despite $20.4M of restructuring and impairment costs; Electronics operating income alone rose 74.3% to $86.9M. Net income rose 55.9% to $89.4M and diluted EPS rose to $3.49 from $2.30, helped by a lower 23.6% tax rate and a swing to a $0.2M FX gain from a $10.4M FX loss a year ago. Cash rose to $628.2M; the dividend rose 7% to $0.80. No forward guidance was given.

drivers.explanation: Revenue growth accelerated on the Basler acquisition and stronger Electronics volume, while margin expansion from volume leverage and favorable mix drove profit growth well ahead of sales.
20.4% y/y growth includes $35.8M from the Basler acquisition, $4.1M of favorable FX, and higher electronics products ($44.7M) and semiconductor ($26.1M) volume on demand and price.
Gross margin rose 360bp to 41.4% on volume leverage, operational execution, and favorable mix in Electronics and industrial circuit protection, plus Basler's higher gross margin.

GAAP operating income rose 29.0% on higher gross profit, partly offset by $47.1M higher opex including $20.4M of restructuring/impairment/integration costs. The KPI value ($139.7M) is Yahoo's operating-income method, which nets out those one-time items and tracks closer to segment-level operating income ($140.1M) than the GAAP total.
Not a line the filing discloses directly; this is Yahoo's own EBIT computation and isn't reconcilable to a single 10-Q line, so treat it as directional only.
The filing does not disclose an EBITDA figure; this is Yahoo's GAAP-based EBITDA, which moves with the same operating-income items noted above including one-time restructuring/impairment charges.

Net income rose 55.9% on higher operating income plus a lower effective tax rate (23.6% vs 26.7%) from statute-of-limitations lapses and share-comp tax benefits, and a swing to a $0.2M FX gain from a $10.4M FX loss a year ago.
EPS grew roughly in step with net income; diluted share count was little changed y/y.
EPS grew roughly in step with net income; basic share count was little changed y/y.
